svg.text: The continuous query — one row, two values, and the sink contract
2 // Two of a row's five columns are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = the GROUP BY column
5 type Row { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 rows, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late one
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the TUMBLE size, in seconds. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: PERIOD — the HOP slide, in seconds. PERIOD = 60
11 // primitive: GAP — the SESSION gap, in seconds. GAP = 120
12 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
13 // primitive: KEYS — the distinct GROUP BY values. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
14 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
15 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those row ids.
17 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest et through i, minus LAG.
23 // primitive: W0 — the window this trace follows. W0 = 0 ([12:00, 12:02))
24 // primitive: bucketOf(row) — the TUMBLE bucket, read off the et column.
27 // function: upsert(sink, bucket, value) — the UPDATING sink: one row per bucket,
28 // overwritten. An INSERT-only sink cannot express this.
29 // upsert(sink, W0, 15) then upsert(sink, W0, 19) leaves 19 after 2 writes
36 // function: insertOnly(sink, bucket, value) — the APPEND-ONLY sink, for contrast:
37 // it adds rather than replaces, so a revision double-counts.
38 // insertOnly(sink, W0, 15) then insertOnly(sink, W0, 19) leaves 34
46 // function: run(canUpsert) — the engine: accumulate, emit when the watermark
47 // closes the bucket, and re-emit on every later row for that bucket.
56 if (watermarkAfter(i) < W0 + WIN && fired == false) { continue }
58 if (canUpsert == false) { sink = insertOnly(sink, W0, sum(ids)) }
64 // function: main() — THE CALLER: the same query into two kinds of sink.
Step 3/0 — id 7 arrives and the SAME row is written again
`sink.rows[0] = 19` — an assignment, replacing 15. `writes` reaches 2 for one logical result, which is what "updating stream" means in practice: the sink
is written more often than the answer changes meaning.
